title: Flask default session cookie signs content but does not provide confidentiality
summary: Flask stores the default session in a client cookie and signs it for integrity. A readable cookie can still reject modifications.
applies: Flask default configuration; request and session data explanation
detail: Just seeing a string of encoded cookies cannot determine that the server has saved independent session records of the same value.
boundary: A custom SessionInterface or server-side session extension might just put the identifier in the cookie.
relevance: Identify what data the browser and server each hold in the sample application.
